questions.solution_html:
• Compare Pierre Sorline's and Natalie Zemon Davies's historiographical methods.
  • Sorline focuses on film as a document of the time it was produced, while Davies treats film as a legitimate historical tool that
  • can supplement textual evidence if handled with professional rigor.

questions.solution_html:
• Discuss an important manner in which filmic representation differs from textual.
  • Filmic representation is audio-visual and multi-sensory, allowing for "simultaneity" (multiple events in one frame), whereas
  • textual representation is typically linear and analytical.

  • or personalities - Cannot distort facts when audiences are familiar with the plot - They

  • linked to national pride, any sort of imagination that distorts facts may provoke political
  • and social reactions

questions.question: In What ways can different modes of Emplotment (romance ,tragedy, comedy,satire)influence the interpretation in Film History. / [CO2] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• In What ways can different modes of Emplotment (romance, tragedy, comedy,
  • satire) influence the interpretation in Film History. [E] / [CO2]
  • Hayden White defines emplotment as the process of turning historical events into a
  • structured narrative. Historians do not just record facts; they shape them into meaningful
  • stories using literary structures. The same historical events can be told in different ways
  • depending on the emplotment chosen - The film Iyyobinte Pusthakam intertwines
  • protagonist’s romantic relationship with his fight for justice, in the backdrop of British
  • colonization. The film Chemmeen reflects the tragic consequences of caste, tradition, and
  • superstition within a marginalized community, offering insight into historical social
  • structures. The film Sandesham uses satire and comedy to expose the absurdities of
  • political ideologies and party rivalries.
